transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CloudVendorX PM), Ben Turner (Marketplace Eng), Liu Wei (Solutions Architect), Marta Silva (Biz Ops)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we know folks are on different time zones so appreciate it. quick agenda — marketplace listing, ref arch for the private offering, and then next steps for joint demo.
[00:10] Aisha: thanks Jordan, yeah we want to get clear on the technical reqs so our marketplace team can move forward — also curious about packaging options, whether we need a dedicated private deployment or can do marketplace-managed hosting.
[00:20] Priya: right. so Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private. for marketplace we typically provide a container image plus helm chart and optional terraform modules for infra. customers can choose to deploy in their VPC or use our hosted offering linked via a peering option.
[00:34] Ben: is there a preference from marketplace side — like do you prefer a BYO infra model or a managed listing where we host it? because that affects billing and how the marketplace meter hooks work.
[00:45] Jordan: good question. we are flexible — for this partner i think a marketplace listing that enables both is ideal: listing points to the terraform/helm for BYO, and then a separate managed offering for customers who want redwood-hosted. but we need the marketplace listing copy to differentiate.
[01:02] Liu: for the private path, network was our main concern. VPC peering, routing, and how KV cache persists, plus KMS integration for customer keys. can you describe how Redwood handles KMS/HSM?
[01:15] Marco: sure — we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) for data-at-rest and to encrypt model artifacts and keys. for on-prem or air-gapped we have an HSM integration pattern; i'll share the HSM reference in the docs. note: our runtime keeps KV cache ephemeral unless customer configures persistent cache with encrypted storage.
[01:36] Marta: is SOC2 material needed for marketplace listing? our legal flagged that.
[01:40] Jordan: yes SOC 2 and ISO certs are usually required for enterprise listings. we will share our compliance pack — SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and the SSO/SAML integration guide.
[01:52] Ben: regarding images — do you sign images? marketplace requires signed images and a vulnerability scan report.
[01:58] Priya: we do sign release images and we can provide SBOM and scan reports for the images we publish. for partner-specific images we recommend your CI sign them and we can validate the signature in the deployment script.
[02:12] Aisha: great. another question: what's the recommended reference architecture for customers that want low latency and data residency? we need an example diagram to put in the listing.
[02:22] Marco: typical pattern is a VPC-hosted Redwood runtime in the customer's region, with model shard(s) pinned for latency, prefix caching enabled, and an optional outbound egress to Redwood telemetry endpoints if customer allows. we have a diagram where the serving runtime sits in private subnets, ingress via ALB or NLB, and a dedicated peering to our control plane if needed. i'll attach the diagram.
[02:44] Liu: do you have terraform snippets for the peering and the IAM roles? that would speed up our internal approvals.
[02:50] Priya: yes — terraform + helm snippets. they include the minimal IAM roles for S3/Key management and the kube service account bindings. we'll redact production secrets in the example.
[03:05] Ben: billing — marketplace expects metering hooks. if we do BYO, the partner needs to call Redwood metering API or we'll need a marketplace-friendly meter. what's the flow?
[03:16] Jordan: for BYO, the deployment can push usage metrics to the marketplace via a marketplace connector, or we can send usage to your billing endpoint if there's a contract. for managed offerings we integrate with the marketplace's metering APIs directly. i'll coordinate with your billing contact.
[03:30] Marta: timeline question — our GTM team wants a joint demo for partners by Mar 25. is that feasible?
[03:36] Jordan: yes, if we get the helm chart and test staging infra by next week we can run a joint demo. action items: we'll send checklist today; Redwood SEs will provision staging and run perf sanity tests.
[03:52] Aisha: any known blockers for marketplace approval processes? sometimes they want a self-hosted install path validated.
[03:58] Priya: main blockers are usually image signing, SBOM, and a documented install flow. also clear network diagrams showing no inbound rules that expose secrets. we'll provide a hardened install guide.
[04:12] Ben: one more: do you support SAML just-in-time provisioning? marketplace customers often want SSO integration.
[04:18] Marco: yes SAML and OIDC are supported; we'll share a sample SAML metadata and the attributes we need. there might be some field name mismatches with the marketplace — small mapping work.
[04:29] Liu: about the reference arch doc — can you include an example of quantization/optimizations config? customers ask about cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:36] Priya: we can include recommended quantization profiles and the tradeoffs matrix — e.g. int8 gives 2-3x throughput improvement at some quality delta; we'll provide suggested eval prompts.
[04:48] Aisha: great, that will help GTM copy too.
[04:52] Jordan: to recap the deliverables — Jordan: share marketplace listing checklist and draft listing copy by Mar 14; Priya to share helm/terraform snippets and ref arch diagram by Mar 18; Marco to run staging perf tests and send logs by Mar 26; Ben to send marketplace constraints by Mar 17. Schedule joint demo for Mar 25 — Jordan and Marta will coordinate.
[05:15] Marta: i'll follow up with calendar invites and loop in GTM.
[05:19] Ben: one nit — image vulnerability scan cadence, how often do you run scans on your published images?
[05:25] Priya: we run automated scans on every release and are happy to provide a recent report. for partner images we recommend they run daily scans and publish SBOMs.
[05:35] Jordan: any other questions?
[05:38] Aisha: i'm good. thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[05:41] Liu: thanks. we'll start internal approvals and share the network diagram.
[05:45] Jordan: perfect. i'll send the checklist and draft copy after the call. thanks all.
[05:50] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had a few misheard acronyms (e.g., KV cache transcribed as "kay-vee" sometimes) and occasional speaker attribution swaps; technical terms preserved mostly intact. Some timestamps are approximate.
